premise: I emptied my $100,000 retirement fund to co‑found a tiny‑home construction company with my son‑in‑law after he signed a 40% equity share and promised me the first model home as a lifetime cottage; he forged a release, sold the company and its blueprints for $750,000, and handed me a $6,000 ‘settlement.’ I proved the forgery with a time‑stamped video of our handshake deal, won the company and the model home, and now run ‘Small Lies Tiny Homes’ — he’s court‑ordered to tighten screws on display models in a shirt that says ‘Built on Deceit,’ and every tiny‑home manual links to the fraud judgment.
